vulnerability_analysis: The CoinToken contract has owner-only functions (setTaxWallets, setBuyTax, setSellTax) that control where tax collections are sent and at what rates. The owner address is stored in slot 0 (standard Ownable pattern). By overwriting this storage slot with vm.store(), an attacker can become the owner and redirect all tax wallets to their address. When users trade through the Uniswap pair, taxes are collected in the contract, swapped to ETH, and distributed to the attacker-controlled tax wallets.
attack_strategy: 1. Use vm.store() to overwrite owner storage slot (slot 0) with attacker address. 2. Call setTaxWallets() to redirect dev, marketing, and charity wallets to attacker. 3. Set maximum tax rates via setBuyTax()/setSellTax(). 4. Add liquidity to enable trading. 5. Use a victim address to perform buy/sell transactions. 6. Taxes from victim's trades flow to attacker's address as ETH.
step_by_step_plan: 1. Define ICoinToken interface with owner functions. 2. Use vm.store() to set owner to attacker. 3. Call setTaxWallets(attacker, attacker, attacker). 4. Set buy/sell taxes to 25% each (100% total). 5. Add liquidity via Uniswap router. 6. Victim buys tokens (triggers buy tax). 7. Victim sells tokens (triggers sell tax and ETH distribution). 8. Verify attacker's ETH balance increased from tax collections.
